inscription: 8 [three figures, tops sheared by the paper edge] ... G.
notes: Two marks in fine pen along the paper edge, upright in the lower panel. Left: a plain 8 followed by three strokes whose upper halves the paper edge has taken; what survives could be 121, 111 or 12 with a flourish, and I will not choose between them. Right, well separated: a large looped capital with a full stop after it, most like G., presumably an initial. e5 carries a separate pencil mark at the edge reading 413 or 4 13, again clipped at the top, which could be a roll number or an abbreviated month and year. No date can be settled from any of it. e2 to e4 are bare paper.

No digits are present in it. e3 has a small cross-shaped mark and an ink blot near the edge, neither of them writing; e2 and e4 hold nothing.

No punch date, and no part of the label's writing is legible enough to record.
